## How they got there
Arsenal reached the final as runners-up after losing to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties, finishing with a 1-1 draw and a 3-4 penalty shootout result. Their profile during the group phase was defined by exceptional efficiency, boasting a points per game of 3.0 which placed them better than 100% of that season's teams, alongside a goal difference per game of 2.38 where they were also better than 100% of their peers.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would have selected Arsenal as a finalist, ranking them second among all knockout teams with a probability of 25.6%. This figure is significantly higher than the base rate of 8.3%, indicating that while the team's actual performance was outstanding, the statistical profile suggests an expectation nearest to reaching the semi-finals rather than the final itself.

## Weak spots
Arsenal had no clear weak spot among the last three stats in the list, as they beat fewer than half of teams on none of them; their lowest ranking among the bottom three listed metrics was 36% for long passes (% of passes). The model's negative contributions from passes per game (450), attacks per game (50.1), and distance covered per game (118.5) do not constitute weak spots because the team still outperformed a majority of their league-phase counterparts on these specific metrics.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
